sanghas.name: Peaceful Garden Sangha
sanghas.address: United Parish Church, 210 Harvard Street, Brookline, MA
sanghas.access: Use the Marion Street entrance (up the stairs to the Parlor on the left). Green C line or Bus 66. Or ample free parking on side streets.
sanghas.description: We are a secular group of friends that practice mindful living in the Plum Village tradition. Some are brand new and others of us have an established practice.  We’re peer- led and share in facilitation. While our meetings are based on Buddhist practices, everyone is encouraged to appreciate and deepen their own (root) tradition.  We welcome all ages, identities backgrounds and experience. Each evening we share a reading and talk about what comes up for us. Our practice is interactive.

sanghas.name: Peaceful Songbird Sangha
sanghas.access: For in-person, there's street parking and lot parking behind the temple.
sanghas.description: We meditate, check-in with one another, share a reading from a teacher of the dharma, and follow with Dharma discussion, metta practice and a final meditation. We practice in the Plum Village tradition of Thich Nhat Hanh, with its emphasis on engaged Buddhism and the art of mindful living.All are welcome to join us. Email us: PeacefulSongbird+owner@BostonOldPath.groups.io

sanghas.address: Cambridge Zen Center, 199 Auburn Street, Cambridge, MA
sanghas.access: Conveniently off the red line, with limited metered street parking.
sanghas.description: This Black, Indigenous and People of Color (BIPOC) practice group is a monthly gathering of self-identifying BIPOC practitioners that provides a safe place to meditate and explore contemplative practices. This sangha cultivates an environment that welcomes diverse voices and builds community. In a typical practice group, we enjoy a mix of sitting meditation, walking meditation, readings, and dharma sharing about our experiences and practice in everyday life.
